text:
I was going to get a GTX 1080 Ti, but I've decided on getting it because of DLSS.  No,  it's not out yet, but when it does come (and I know this is solely on the promise of Nvidia),
but straight up lying to people would be tantamount to giving AMD all their secrets and killing the company.  I believe them.  You might say, well look at the Ray Tracing
performance.  It was on an RTX 2080 Ti and they only got 60 FPS playing BFV on 1080p and yeah, I totally agree.  If people are  buying it for RT, then they are going to be REALLY disappointed, but Nvidia didn't lie.  Ray Tracing will be the shit around the RTX 40xx series, but now....no way.  So, why get it?  As I said, DLSS.  To over simplify it, it's anti-aliasing on steroids, plus 64x supersampling the image up to 4k.  I don't know what older games will get it, but the games that I want will get it and the games that don't, then.... they'll run like a GTX 1080 Ti.  If I didn't believe DLSS was going to be a factor, I'd skip it.  I just don't believe Nvidia is going to try to lie or trick everyone.  They won't get away with it if they tried something like that and as overpriced as they are, they're worth it.  What I'm pissed about is the price of the 1080 Ti.  If they had the 1080 Ti $600 or less (which they might on BF and CM), but I'm looking toward the future.  I won't be upgrading for a long time.

Another thing to consider is driver optimization.  The RTX drivers will get better over time.  This is almost like starting over in a sense, like when the GeForce was first released.  It's not quite that dramatic of a difference when the  GeForce 256 was first released, but they're balancing GTX and RTX all on the same driver.  Of course the priority is going toward the RTX cards, but they can't "slow down" the pascal and older cards either.  It's not like I wouldn't put it past Nvidia, because I know they're past.  I'm old. My first computer was the Commodore=64, the original.  I was around 12 I think.  

Remember Apple getting busted for intentionally slowing down older iPhones.  I don't know what happened with that, other than, they reversed it, but the people that were affected should have been given their choice of either the iPhone X or $1000.  These companies think people are stupid and won't know the difference.  Not the enthusiasts.  If I had an older iPhone I sure would have.  Anyway, for those of you that are getting a 1080 Ti instead, I completely understand.  I was originally going to get an RTX 2070.  I have a GTX 1070 right now and while the 2070 is faster than the 1070, I'm just VERY unhappy with the RT crap.
